sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *quien* from B1 Unit 5, and *donde* for places. They add information about a person, an idea or an organisation without starting a new sentence. They help to describe who proposed the market reforms and what they said.

items.spanish: Son ideas económicas que dan más importancia al mercado.
items.english: These are economic ideas that give more importance to the market.

items.spanish: John Williamson es el economista que acuñó el término «Consenso de Washington».
items.english: John Williamson is the economist who coined the term “Washington Consensus”.

items.spanish: El FMI y el Banco Mundial son organismos que pedían estas reformas.
items.english: The IMF and the World Bank are organisations that asked for these reforms.

items.spanish: Chile es uno de los países donde las reformas empezaron antes.
items.english: Chile is one of the countries where the reforms began earlier.

items.spanish: Carlos Menem es el presidente con quien se asocian las privatizaciones argentinas.
items.english: Carlos Menem is the president with whom the Argentine privatisations are associated.

sections.content: Use *que* for people, things and ideas, *donde* for places, and *quien* after a preposition when the noun is a person (*con quien*). The relative clause follows the noun it describes. Commas add extra information: *Menem, que fue presidente de Argentina, …*.
